not re-proved before every Git process: racing a path swap is deliberate

this store's own compare-and-swap, no do-math writer can have moved the

idempotent: an existing loose object is kept, and a concurrent writer of

Enter a just-published candidate as its head's validated read.

reading the head back would re-prove the same facts. Its payload

Like :meth:`load`, but return the shared validated state without copying it.

The validated (instance, runtime) this process holds for ``head``, or None.

Validate and atomically publish once, returning the published normalized views.

The candidate must have been validated against ``expected_head``. Any
other candidate is validated in full first, as :meth:`save_with_state` would.

``parent`` is an (instance, runtime) pair already validated under this
contract. A record equal to the parent's record at the same family and
ID skips the record-local checks (schema and family validator), whose
result depends on the record alone. Relations, identity uniqueness and
semantic rules are still checked over the whole state.

Equality is Python ``==``, under which ``1 == 1.0 == True``. A float
cannot pass: payloads.seal_large rejects every float of a candidate
before this comparison. A bool swapped for an equal integer (or back)
in a record otherwise equal to the parent's is an accepted gap: it
skips that record's schema check and keeps the parent's bytes
(repository._encode_families). A type-strict comparison would walk
every node in Python, about 27 times the cost of ``==`` on a 3.6 MB
state, twice per save.

Shared toolchain records: installation identity, fingerprints and content baselines.

One record file describes one installed Lean/Mathlib identity. setup_lean.py
writes it when a toolchain is installed or replaced, re-recorded or explicitly
content-checked; research instances only read it. The threat model is
accidental change (updates, reinstallation, synchronization, mistakes, disk
damage). A fingerprint row is the scandir metadata of one judgment file, so
bytes changed while size and both times are preserved are found only by an
explicit content check against the recorded full hashes.

The OS releases the lock when its holder ends, so a killed writer leaves nothing to remove.

An environment copies the identity of one shared toolchain record and names
the record file. The runtime binding names the record baseline whose olean
fingerprint this instance last accepted. Checks cover accidental change only;
they do not isolate the checker from a writer with the same OS identity.

until the toolchain record or the active environment changes.

This module owns process lifetime and optional local resource caps. A Job does not isolate files,
network, IPC, credentials, or process identity; those boundaries need separate
enforcement.

A single suspended root atomically placed in a kill-on-close Job.

The object is the sole holder of its non-inheritable Job handle.  Closing
it therefore kills remaining roots and descendants.  It intentionally

Sequential shard-by-shard unittest runner with owned, bounded Lean/resource workers.

Tests are selected by ID or module (positional), by shard (``--shard``), or all
shards when neither is given. Every selected test runs; there is no result cache.
Shards and the isolation labels live in ``test_categories.py`` beside this runner; a test
module missing from ``SHARDS`` stops the run. When and what to run is in
``tests/시험-지침.md``.

Lean and resource tests run per class in an owned Windows Job with a per-phase
deadline. Normal unittest discovery still works but imposes no outer deadlines.
This runner never changes the product's Lean time limits.

symbols.doc: Each test and the surrounding fixture/shutdown phase has its own limit.

Prepare the machine-wide Lean toolchain and record it for the research instances.

Installation is idempotent: finished steps are skipped. A toolchain record is written
only after `import Mathlib` compiles through the exact command the verifier will use,
and the ready marker follows the record, so a half-downloaded cache is never selected.
Record writers (installation, --verify-only, --rerecord, --check-contents) exclude each
other with the lock file of the records directory. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 a refused,
failed or mismatching result, 2 an execution error. Every mode prints one JSON object on stdout;
installation progress and Lake output go to stderr.

A baseline is compared by metadata later, so it must not record a time that a

Shards and isolation labels for do-math tests.

``SHARDS`` is the one list of which test module runs in which shard;
``run_tests.py`` refuses to run while a ``tests/test_*.py`` module is missing
from it or it names a module that does not exist. The time targets (each shard
alone within 120 s, all shards in sequence within 300 s) and when to run what
are in ``tests/시험-지침.md``.

``test_group('lean')`` and ``test_group('resource')`` mark tests that call the
real Lean toolchain or manage real process lifetimes and resources; the runner
runs them per class in an owned Windows Job with a deadline. A label goes on
the class when every test in it needs isolation, otherwise on each such method;
a method's label overrides its class's.

symbols.doc: 'lean' or 'resource' when the test must run isolated, else None; a method label overrides its class.

files.doc:
Engine doubles and the engine start states tests share.

Two kinds of engine appear here. Both are the product ``ResearchEngine``:

- In-memory engines hold supplied state and publish nothing to Git.
  ``FakeEngine(root, config=None)`` is an initialized instance ``RI-test`` over
  the ``StateStore`` double whose ``_save`` records copies in ``saves``; it
  grants, registers synthetic trust environments, activates through the
  adoption decision (``activate``), creates knowledge and approved tasks, and
  processes one queued machine action (``machine``). ``approve_contract`` and
  ``formal_verification`` are its contract review and compiler double for
  records outside it; ``formal_check_engine(test)`` is one with a candidate and
  its queued formal check. ``routing_engine()`` is a bare engine with an empty
  active-looking instance for response routing; ``intent_import`` and
  ``intent_verdict`` author and check one interpretation on it.
  ``context_engine(instance=None, runtime=None)`` keeps the real role-context
  producer over ``record_fixtures.surface_state``; ``package`` prepares one
  role input with it. ``initial_failure_engine`` holds a failed initial
  interpretation waiting for maintenance. ``reassessment_engine`` holds a task
  waiting for a missing input. ``governance_host`` and ``goal_audit_host`` hold
  checked governance changes. ``evidence_engine`` is an active instance whose
  store is ``input_snapshot_store``; ``reviewed_task``, ``apply_plan``,
  ``accept_knowledge`` and ``audit_goal`` drive it.
- Git-backed start states give a ``unittest.TestCase`` its attributes.
  ``start_submission_history(test)`` puts a running maintenance execution with
  a sealed input on a copy of the validated active state
  (``state_fixtures.start_active_copy``); ``submit_history`` delivers its
  submission intent and ``start_native_final`` adds its decision basis.
  ``start_query_repository(test)`` publishes knowledge records and a relation
  through the public ``initialize``. ``start_repair_host(test)`` gives a bare
  engine over a real repository that holds one pending operational retry.
  ``initialized`` and the template build ``initialized_instance`` run the
  public ``initialize`` alone; ``PublicInitializationRunner`` answers its
  interpretation roles.

``native_result`` is a provider's native final output for a registered
execution, as the runner reports it; it creates no process.

(its tasks and ready task IDs). It has no Git directory, so no process

files.doc:
Knowledge candidates, their synthetic formal evidence and small knowledge states.

Compiler results here are explicit doubles (``formal_result``), never a Lean
run; identity assessments are recorded directly, never reviewed.

- ``knowledge_candidate(**changes)``: the theorem candidate "Truth"
  (``theorem truth : True := True.intro``); ``changes`` replace its fields.
- ``formal_result(source, declarations, toolchain, ...)``: a verified compiler
  result for ``source``; every declaration depends on ``closure`` and carries
  the given dependency and declaration evidence strings.
- ``formal_evidence(state, kid, env='TE-old')``: ``formal_result`` for the
  stored formal record of ``kid`` under trust environment ``env``.
- ``seal_knowledge(state, runtime, kid, env='TE-old')``: record that evidence and a
  matching identity assessment; returns ``(state, assessment ID)``.
- ``add_knowledge(state, runtime, *, verified=True, **changes)``: import a
  candidate and seal it; returns ``(state, runtime, kid, assessment ID)``.
- ``knowledge_graph()``: ``(state, runtime, ids)``, three sealed records ``a``,
  ``b`` (depends on ``a``) and ``c`` with a relation ``a``→``c``, a current goal
  judgment using ``b`` and completed tasks using ``b`` and ``c``.
- ``impact_declaration(state, runtime, roots)``: the complete computed impact a
  producer declares; ``revise_knowledge`` revises one record with it.
- ``activate_kind(state, token, family='relation', definition=None)``: register,
  check and activate one kind definition.
- ``verified_knowledge(environment=None, *, binding=None, identity=True)``:
  ``(state, runtime, kid, assessment ID)``, the candidate verified under
  ``TE-test`` and (unless ``identity=False``) assessed as a match.
- ``formal_boundary_engine(workspace, toolchain=None)``: ``(engine, kid)``, a
  bare engine with an adopted trust environment ``TE-old`` (the installed
  ``toolchain`` when given, else a synthetic one) and one unverified candidate
  whose formal check replaces admission, storage and review start with autospec
  doubles; its verifier returns ``formal_evidence``.

symbols.name: formal_result
symbols.doc: A verified compiler result for ``source``; ``extra`` adds fields such as ``allowed_axioms``.

files.doc:
Doubles at the provider, host-process and external-service boundaries.

Nothing here starts a model, a Lean compiler or a network service of its own.
Each double stands where the product reaches something outside the process:

- Model runner: ``Adapter`` is a scripted provider collector for a real
  ``ModelRunner`` (``runner_with``); ``mock_adapter`` is a bare Mock with the
  provider's real worker options. ``Job`` and ``Execution`` are the process
  handles ``Adapter.start`` returns. ``FakeJob`` answers ``inspect`` with a
  fixed ``JobInspection``.
- Claude stream: ``claude_stream(*events)`` encodes JSONL rows;
  ``CLAUDE_INIT`` and ``CLAUDE_RESULT`` are the first and last rows of a
  successful run.
- Provider limits over session slots: ``provider_repository(root)`` initializes
  one ready instance in the Git repository at ``root`` whose three tiers all use
  ``PROVIDER_MODEL`` (three work slots). ``admit`` registers and admits one
  execution, ``report`` applies a synthetic runner result (a
  ``PROVIDER_LIMIT_FAILURE`` or a completed call), ``finish`` releases and ends
  it, and ``transact`` runs one such operation under the writer lock and saves.
  ``instant`` turns epoch seconds into the ISO time the records use.
- Execution profiles: ``PROFILE_CONFIG`` is a complete profile configuration
  for ``build_profiles``; ``host_capacity_fixture()`` adds an approved host
  constraint and host-bounded work, recovery and formal-check profiles.
- Lean: ``actual_command()`` is the installed compiler command
  (``DO_MATH_KNOWLEDGE_TEST_LEAN`` overrides it); only ``lean``-labelled tests call it.
- HTTP: ``HTTPFixtureHandler`` answers POST with 201 and GET with a redirect.

symbols.name: Adapter
symbols.doc: A scripted collector; the worker request fields are its provider's real ones.

symbols.name: mock_adapter
symbols.doc: A Mock adapter whose worker request fields are its provider's real ones.

symbols.name: runner_with
symbols.doc: A ModelRunner that starts ``adapter`` for ``provider``'s models.

symbols.name: FakeJob
symbols.doc: A job whose ``inspect`` reports ``state``.

symbols.name: provider_repository
symbols.doc: Initialize one ready instance in the Git repository at ``root``; returns its ``ResearchRepository``.

symbols.name: admit
symbols.doc: Admit a work role (a model slot) or an operational role such as maintenance (no slot).

symbols.name: report
symbols.doc: Apply a synthetic runner result: a provider_limit failure, or a completed call.

symbols.name: host_capacity_fixture
symbols.doc:
``(instance, selected, constraint)``: ``PROFILE_CONFIG`` profiles under an approved host constraint.

``selected`` maps research_work, recovery and formal_check to a profile
that reserves one job, 128 MiB and 20% CPU of ``constraint``.

symbols.name: HTTPFixtureHandler
symbols.doc: POST answers 201 ``ok``; GET redirects to another origin.

files.doc:
The purpose scenario: a scripted research run that proves one natural-number identity.

``PurposeRunner(scenario='direct', observation=None)`` answers every role from
its actual input: preparation proposes task ``A`` (a formal theorem, ``SOURCE``),
review approves, work returns ``theorem()``, identity review matches and the
goal audit is satisfied once a certified result exists. ``scenario`` selects
variants (``dependency``: ``B`` before ``A``; ``dispute``: one withdrawn
objection; ``currentness``: a downstream task that consumes the result;
``catalog``: a long report); ``observation`` drives live observation of the
first work call (``continue``, ``stop``, ``external_pause``). ``formal_fixture``
is its compiler double, which covers ``SOURCE`` only. ``parse_context``,
``common``, ``candidate`` and ``theorem`` are the pieces of its answers;
``GOAL``, ``STATEMENT``, ``EXPLANATION`` and ``NEW_GOAL`` are its texts.
``AcademicRunner`` extends it with academic tasks, resolutions and external
effects; ``CheckedRunner`` wraps a runner so that its output passes the
producer check and control transport as a worker's does.

Harnesses
---------
``PurposeHarness`` holds the scenario's configuration (``fixture_config``) and
``drive(engine, predicate=None, limit=45)``, which steps the engine until
``predicate`` (default: the goal is mathematically solved) and fails the test
if the flow stops first. ``ActivatedPurposeHarness`` hands out template copies
(``make``: the public activation; ``make_active(**config)``: the validated
synthetic active state), one live copy at a time.

Template builds (``research_fixtures.restore_template``)
--------------------------------------------------------
- ``solved_instance(root, shared, *, criteria)``: the public activation driven to
  the mathematical solution; ``criteria`` approves requirement ``writeup``
  (``requirement``) first. It returns the instance ID, the head the driving
  engine published last and the runner's work order. ``drive_to`` is the
  build's bounded drive.
- ``purpose_state(root, shared, *, config, until, ...)``: the synthetic active
  state driven until task ``A``'s work is queued (``until='prepared'``) or its
  identity review opens (``'review'``); ``purpose_copy`` gives a harness test
  an engine on a copy.
- ``assessment_preparation_instance(root, shared, *, config)``: two academic
  tasks awaiting model assessment; ``prepared_assessment_engine`` gives a
  harness test an engine on a copy with ``ASSESSMENT_CONFIG``.
``CURRENTNESS_CONFIG`` is the configuration of the currentness scenarios.

symbols.name: PurposeHarness
symbols.doc: The purpose scenario's configuration (``fixture_config``) and its bounded ``drive``.

symbols.name: ActivatedPurposeHarness
symbols.doc:
``PurposeHarness`` whose instances are copies of templates built once per process.

``make`` hands out the state the public ``initialize`` and ``activate``
publish for the scenario (``research_fixtures.activated_instance`` with
``fixture_config``), restored byte for byte (``research_fixtures.restore_template``);
``make_active`` does the same for the validated synthetic active state
(``state_fixtures.active_instance``) with the given configuration. Only
the engine object is new, as after a restart. Each call replaces the
previous copy, so a test holds one live instance at a time.

symbols.name: AcademicRunner
symbols.doc: Purpose fixture that supplies an explicit planner resolution when asked.

symbols.name: drive_to
symbols.doc: ``PurposeHarness.drive`` for a template build, which has no test case to fail.

symbols.name: solved_instance
symbols.doc:
``restore_template`` build: public activation, then the real mathematical solution.

This is the public ``initialize`` and ``activate`` (``activated_instance``)
followed by driving to ``mathematically_solved``. ``criteria`` None solves
without academic requirements, so the runtime completes. A list approves
requirement ``writeup`` with those criteria first, so the solution generates
its academic task through the real path and the runtime stays open.
``AcademicRunner`` answers like ``PurposeRunner`` until an academic task or
an academic rejection exists. Returns ``{'instance_id', 'head', 'work_order'}``:
the head the driving engine published last and the order in which the
runner answered research work.

symbols.name: purpose_state
symbols.doc:
``restore_template`` build: synthetic active state advanced by ``PurposeRunner('direct')``.

``until='prepared'``: task A is prepared, its contract approved and the plan
selected it; its ``research_work`` is queued. ``until='review'``: A's work
returned the theorem, its formal check passed and its identity review cycle
opened; the scope review is queued with whatever else the flow queued.
``signed`` checks formally with ``signed_formal_fixture``, else ``formal_fixture``.
Formal checks need ``lean_command=list(ACTIVE_LEAN_COMMAND)`` in ``config``.
Returns the instance ID.

symbols.name: purpose_copy
symbols.doc: Engine and ``runner`` on a fresh copy of ``purpose_state`` for an ``ActivatedPurposeHarness`` test.

symbols.name: CheckedRunner
symbols.doc: Script only the model answer; use actual producer and control protocols.

symbols.name: assessment_preparation_instance
symbols.doc:
``restore_template`` build: two academic tasks of requirement ``r`` without model assessments.

The validated synthetic active state supplies grants; a public charter
control supplies the requirement and its pending event history. The tasks
and their contract reviews are injected, and the published readiness has
replaced the reviews with one assessment-only preparation.

symbols.name: prepared_assessment_engine
symbols.doc: An engine for ``test`` (an ``ActivatedPurposeHarness``) on a copy of ``assessment_preparation_instance``.

files.doc:
Records for tests of pure domain functions: governance, task contracts, submissions.

Each function returns new plain records (dicts); none opens a repository or
runs an engine. Records carry explicit synthetic approvals and evidence, never
an actual user decision or model judgment.

Governance
----------
- ``domain_governance()``: instance ``I`` whose charter ``CH1`` (goal "Prove P")
  the user adopted in decision ``D`` from source ``S``
  (``research_fixtures.approved_governance``).
- ``governance_import()``: ``(instance, runtime, source, output)``, an
  interpretation of the public input ``IN`` into one unit ``U`` that asks one
  optional question ``Q``; ``source`` is that input's exact source.
- ``checked_import(kind='charter', handlers=None, payload=None)``:
  ``(instance, runtime, bundle, request)``, that interpretation changed to
  propose ``payload`` (default: charter ``CH2``, goal "Prove Q", superseding
  ``CH1``), independently checked, waiting for the user's later exact approval
  ``request``.
- ``audited_governance()``: ``(instance, runtime)`` with an active additional
  goal audit ``AU`` over ``CH1``.
- ``applied_initial_intent(text)``: ``(instance, runtime, bundle ID)``, a newly
  initialized instance whose original input ``text`` was interpreted, checked
  and applied to its adopted charter.

Task contracts
--------------
- ``task_contract()``: the planned contract ``TK-1`` with obligations ``OB-1``
  (evidence ``EV-1``) and ``OB-2``.
- ``approved_task()``: ``(task, instance, runtime)``, ``task_contract`` as a
  nonformal task of ``domain_governance`` with one source ``SO-1``, one work
  profile and grant, and an approved contract review (``approve_task``).
- ``task_disposition(identifier, kind='selected')``: one plan disposition row.
- ``transfer_assessment()``: ``(instance, runtime, assessment)``, ``approved_task``
  returned with ``EV-1``, a user decision ``DC-1`` transferring ``OB-2`` to
  ``TK-2``, and the plan assessment that closes ``TK-1`` by that transfer;
  ``apply_assessment`` applies an assessment as the plan execution ``EX-plan``.
- ``completed_with_knowledge()``: ``(instance, runtime)`` after a completed
  assessment of ``TK-1`` that cites a candidate theorem ``KN-proof``.
- ``specialist_assessment(judge='identity_review')``: ``transfer_assessment``
  whose single obligation is judged by ``judge`` and a verified theorem
  (``knowledge_fixtures.verified_knowledge``) cited as its evidence.
- ``withdrawable_task()``: ``(instance, runtime, input_tasks)``, an approved
  AI-prepared task ``TK-AI`` with a dependent, a queued review and a waiting
  work action; ``withdraw_prepared`` withdraws it as the plan ``EX-plan``.
- ``installation_repair_state()``: ``(runtime, record)``, a failed plan
  execution held for an accepted installation repair diagnosis.
- ``contract_check(title='one', **changes)``: one preparation self-check row;
  ``preparation_issues(entries, candidates=..., context=preparation_context(), workspace=...)``
  is the receiver's issue list for a preparation output carrying those checks.

Submissions and surfaces
------------------------
- ``execution_state(role='formal_check')``: ``(instance, runtime)`` under the
  stored lifecycle gate with default profiles and one execution ``EX-1`` of
  ``role`` in activity ``AT-1``.
- ``two_observation_output()``: a research_work output with two independent
  observations in two integration bundles; ``observation_knowledge(title)`` is
  one such row and ``research_work_context()`` its fixed input context.
- ``surface_state()``: ``(instance, runtime)``, ``IN-1`` with an adopted
  charter, default profiles and one running research_work execution ``EX-1``;
  ``stored_surface_state()`` is the same under the stored lifecycle gate.

symbols.name: preparation_context
symbols.doc: The fixed input of a preparation that assesses models (``budget_unit`` concurrent_sessions).

symbols.name: preparation_issues
symbols.doc:
The receiver's issues, as JSON text, for a preparation output proposing ``candidates``.

The extensions carry one model assessment per candidate, the self-checks
``entries``, the task ``conditions`` and the fixture's observation rules
(``research_fixtures.supply_observation_rules``, read at call time, which
adds its rows to ``conditions`` itself); one integration bundle holds them all.

symbols.name: execution_state
symbols.doc: ``(instance, runtime)`` under the lifecycle gate: default profiles and one execution ``EX-1`` of ``role`` in activity ``AT-1``.

symbols.name: stored_surface_state
symbols.doc: surface_state under the current lifecycle gate, as every stored state is.

files.doc:
Shared test fixtures: synthetic inputs, process helpers and shared starting states.

All authority and persistence still pass through the engine. The adapter and
Lean facts here are synthetic test evidence. They do not establish host
capabilities, a real compiler result, or approval by the actual user.

Fixture modules
===============
A test module takes its fixtures from these modules, never from another test
module. Each module's docstring lists what it holds.

- ``research_fixtures`` (this module): inputs every area uses (task
  candidates, review outputs, charters and their approval, trust environments,
  observation rules, clocks and batches), the in-process ``git_init``,
  ``run_cli`` and ``cli_result``, public activation (``activate``) and the
  shared starting states below.
- ``state_fixtures``: the validated synthetic active state (``active_instance``,
  ``active_repository``, ``start_active_copy``) and the owner-loop helpers
  (``owner_calls``, ``start_model_call``).
- ``engine_fixtures``: engine doubles over in-memory state (``FakeEngine``,
  ``routing_engine``, ``context_engine``) and Git-backed engine start states
  (``start_submission_history``, ``start_query_repository``).
- ``runner_fixtures``: ``ScriptedRunner`` and the role outputs it writes.
- ``purpose_fixtures``: the purpose scenario (``PurposeRunner``), its harnesses
  and the builds that drive it.
- ``record_fixtures``: records for pure domain functions (governance, task
  contracts, submissions).
- ``knowledge_fixtures``: knowledge candidates and their synthetic formal evidence.
- ``review_fixtures``: identity review doubles, cycles and harnesses.
- ``provider_fixtures``: provider adapters, host resources and external services.

A fixture that one test module uses stays in that module as a module function.
Before a second module uses it, it moves to the fixture module of its area.

Shared starting states
======================

Building an active instance through the public path (``activate``: several
controls plus two interpretation executions) costs tens of seconds, and a Git
or CLI child process costs a noticeable fraction of a second. A test whose
subject comes after that path starts from a copy of a state built once per
process instead.

What to use
-----------
``restore_template(build, **parameters)`` returns ``(root, value)``. The first
call in a process runs ``build(root, shared, **parameters)`` once. Every call,
the first included, then gives a fresh copy of exactly the bytes that build
left under ``root``: Git objects and refs, the workspace with its ``runs/``
outputs and the control inbox, as the product published them. ``value`` is a
deep copy of what the build returned. Every build puts the repository at
``root / 'repository'`` and the workspace at ``root / 'work-0'``. These builds
are shared (keywords in parentheses):

- ``state_fixtures.active_instance`` (``config``, ``external_policy``,
  ``review_policy``): the validated synthetic active state assembled with
  ``engine_fixtures.FakeEngine``, without interpretation executions;
  returns the instance ID.
- ``activated_instance`` (``goal``, ``config``, ``external_policy``,
  ``review_policy``): public ``initialize`` plus ``activate``, the published
  state before the first research step; returns the instance ID.
- ``engine_fixtures.initialized_instance`` (``goal``, ``config``): the public
  ``initialize`` alone; returns the instance ID.
- ``purpose_fixtures.solved_instance`` (``criteria``): public activation driven
  by the purpose scenario to the mathematical solution, with academic
  requirement ``writeup`` approved first when ``criteria`` is a list; returns
  ``{'instance_id', 'head', 'work_order'}``.
- ``purpose_fixtures.purpose_state`` (``config``, ``until``,
  ``review_policy``, ``external_policy``, ``signed``): the synthetic active
  state driven until task ``A``'s work is queued (``until='prepared'``) or its
  identity review opens (``'review'``); returns the instance ID.
- ``purpose_fixtures.assessment_preparation_instance`` (``config``): two
  academic tasks of requirement ``r`` awaiting model assessment; returns the
  instance ID.

The other builds serve one test module each and stay there, each with its
state in its docstring: ``requirement_change_instance`` (``test_academic_engine``),
``cli_instance`` (``test_cli``), ``created_instance`` (``test_cli_advanced``),
``plan_ready_instance`` (``test_currentness``), ``efficiency_instance``
(``test_engine``), ``overflowed_maintenance`` (``test_input_recovery``),
``rejected_assessment_instance`` (``test_model_assessment_flow``),
``reviewed_task``, ``parked_failed_plan`` and ``paused_limited_recovery``
(``test_research_recovery``), ``ready_work`` (``test_session_scheduler``),
``waiting_action`` (``test_stop_flags``) and ``prepared_tasks``
(``test_submission_boundaries``).

Then ``ResearchEngine(root / 'repository', instance_id, runner=..., formal_verifier=...)``
with a new runner. ``purpose_fixtures.ActivatedPurposeHarness`` wraps the first
two as ``make_active`` and ``make``. ``test_engine.EngineTests.active`` is the
plain form.

Two process helpers replace a child process where the process is not examined:
``git_init(path)`` for ``git init -q <path>`` and ``run_cli(*arguments, cwd=...)``
for ``python do_math.py *arguments`` (a ``CompletedProcess`` with text output).

Rules of a copy
---------------
- ``root`` is the same path for every copy of one template; that keeps the
  absolute paths in the state, and the hashes over them, true. A call replaces
  the previous copy, so a test finishes with one engine before asking for the
  next. A test may add instances to the copied repository itself.
- Parameters are JSON values, and every value that shapes the built state is
  one: goal, config, policies. Set configuration here rather than with a later
  ``configure`` control, which makes new profile editions that need new
  capability evidence. Defaults count, so omitting one names the same template.
- Process-local engine state is not in a copy; set it on the new engine:
  ``_task_readiness`` is empty until ``run`` (call ``_refresh_readiness()`` to
  read it before), and clock or method patches (``lifecycle_clock``,
  ``_solution_basis``) apply to the object they were set on.
- A template lives in one process and is never reused from disk: it carries
  the installed edition, grant expiries (one day after the build) and the
  clock high-water. A test whose rule depends on time elapsed since the build
  uses the public path.
- The build runs inside the first test that asks for it, and a failed build
  fails every later test that asks for the same template.

Writing a build
---------------
``build(root, shared, **parameters)`` creates everything the state names under
``root``, except files whose stat fingerprint the state records, such as
``trust_fixture`` toolchains and records: a copy gets a new creation time, so
those go under ``shared``, which is never copied or cleared and must only be
read afterwards. A deeper state is a build that starts from a ready build on
its own ``root`` (for example ``activated_instance(root, shared, ...)``) and
then drives an engine with a scripted runner; it returns whatever the tests
need (instance IDs, a task's copy before a change, an execution ID). End the
build where no execution is unfinished and nothing is reserved: an executor
started on the copy recovers every unfinished execution. A test that needs a
running call copies the state before it and starts the call itself. Formal
checks on the synthetic state need ``lean_command=list(state_fixtures.ACTIVE_LEAN_COMMAND)``
in its config; public activation registers the configured command itself.

When to keep the public path or the child process
--------------------------------------------------
Keep the public path when the test's subject is that path: initialization,
activation gates, the interpretation check, probes or trust registration
during initialization, or the end-to-end connection the dedicated tests keep
(``test_engine.EngineTests.test_public_initialization_reaches_active_with_distinct_interpretation``,
``test_engine.PublicGitFlow.test_public_activation_work_receipt_assessment_and_next_plan``, and
the ``purpose_fixtures.solved_instance`` build, which ``test_purpose_engine.SolvedPurposeTests``
reads).
Keep it too when the test patches or counts something during activation, or
reads process-local engine state activation leaves behind. The check: if
activation broke while still publishing the same final state, should this
test fail? If yes, it examines the path.

Keep the child process when the process is the subject: exit codes as the
shell sees them, stdout/stderr encoding, ``pythonw``, Windows Jobs, owner
identity of another process, background or detached processes, and the
interpreter's start-up (imports, ``sys.path``, installation freezing). A lock
held by another descriptor in the same process conflicts as across processes
(``file_io.os_lock``), so lock contention alone does not need a child.

When a scenario may stop early
------------------------------
A ``drive``/``run`` loop may stop at the first state in which every asserted
value is final: its predicate is what the assertions read. Before stopping
early, confirm that nothing after that point adds to an asserted count
("exactly N reviews") and that no fixture check that only runs later is lost
(a scripted role that raises on a wrong input is a check). Drive to the goal
when the goal judgment is asserted, is the test's stated claim (its name or
docstring), or feeds such a fixture check.

symbols.name: bare_engine
symbols.doc:
A ``ResearchEngine`` over supplied state, without loading a repository.

The product initializes the process-local owner state, so the engine carries
every attribute a loaded engine has. ``_save`` compares the state with what
``store`` holds for ``head`` (``published_state``); a fixture head the store
never published holds nothing, so the first ``_save`` publishes to ``store``.
Without a ``store`` the engine gets the in-memory ``StateStore`` double.

symbols.name: current_state
symbols.doc:
The smallest (instance, runtime) the current state contract accepts, plus the caller's fields.

Every validated state passes the lifecycle rules (``record_schemas.validate_lifecycle``):
a lifecycle with its exact original input, a runtime status and a UTC clock
high-water. Storage tests extend this with the families they examine.

symbols.name: governance_start
symbols.doc:
``instance`` with the empty governance families ``initialization.initialize_state`` gives every instance.

A domain test that calls a governance function on a small instance starts here
instead of relying on the function to create these families.

symbols.name: installed_contract
symbols.doc:
A new StateContract holding the installed families, for a test that adds to it.

Repositories share default_state_contract(), which never gains a family,
so a test registers extra families on a contract of its own.

symbols.name: with_validator
symbols.doc: Give one family of a test-owned ``contract`` this record validator in place of its own.

symbols.name: StateStore
symbols.doc:
The persisted head of an in-memory engine double.

It implements the repository calls an in-memory engine reaches: ``load``
reads the engine's current state as that head's published state,
``published_state`` holds no cached state (so ``_save`` always publishes),
and ``save_with_state`` publishes a candidate as the next head and keeps a
copy in ``published``. It has no Git directory (``git_dir`` is None), so no
process cache records its reads. Any other repository use fails as it would
without a store.

symbols.name: new_instance
symbols.doc:
Create a Git repository and initialize one instance in it through the public ``initialize``.

``workspace`` defaults to ``repository / 'work'``; ``options`` pass to ``initialize``.
Returns the new instance ID.

symbols.name: read_fixture_context
symbols.doc: Read the same exact local sources exposed to the scripted role.

symbols.name: bind_candidates
symbols.doc: Select only work profiles and current grants actually supplied to the author.

symbols.name: review_items
symbols.doc: A contract review output that reviews every product contract item alike.

symbols.name: Clock
symbols.doc: A settable clock for an ``ObservationTracker``: each call returns ``value``.

symbols.name: observation_rule
symbols.doc:
One observation rule ``R-1`` on ``subject_id``; its basis is ``operator``'s own source and unit.

The default counts ``attempts`` from the worker checkpoint; ``changes``
replace fields (``id``, ``required_evidence``, ``basis``) or add
``repeat_interval``.

symbols.name: self_check_response
symbols.doc:
The worker's answer to a delivered self-check ``obligation``: every due rule gets ``status``.

``evidence`` replaces each rule's required evidence references; an
``indeterminate`` answer names that evidence as missing.

symbols.name: supply_observation_rules
symbols.doc: Declare an explicit checkpoint-counter policy for the scripted short task.

symbols.name: write_checkpoint
symbols.doc: Write a valid worker checkpoint; a tracker reads counters and iterations only from here.

symbols.name: observe
acknowledge
symbols.doc:
Deliver an open self-check request and observe the worker's successful poll of it.

After this, a research action the tracker observes violates the open request.

symbols.name: observation_batch
symbols.doc: The runner's batch of ``events`` as consecutive JSON rows starting at stream offset ``start``.

symbols.name: prepared_rule_conditions
symbols.doc: Explicit response fixture for assigned existing-task rule preparation.

symbols.name: seal_response
symbols.doc: Producer declares its real output/extension coordinates as one coupled unit.

symbols.name: local_job_runner
symbols.doc: Give scripted model calls a real, bounded local process lifetime.

symbols.name: dispatched_launch
symbols.doc: The current explicit runner contract used by native boundary fixtures.

symbols.name: await_control
symbols.doc: Wait until the running owner loop has applied a queued public control.

symbols.name: await_stop
symbols.doc: Wait until the owner's stop judgment has set the calculation's flag.

symbols.name: producer_result
symbols.doc: Add only producer transport/envelope facts to a scenario's explicit response.

symbols.name: FixtureAdapter
symbols.doc: The synthetic observation double for ``LocalCLIAdapter``'s probe surface.

symbols.name: install_adapter_fixture
symbols.doc: Replace only external observation; retain evidence hashing and capability gates.

symbols.name: fixture_setup_lean
symbols.doc:
setup_lean with host observations replaced by a fixture toolchain.

Fixture files are created moments before, so the racy window is closed for
them; recording would otherwise wait for their fingerprints to settle.

symbols.name: validation_fixture
symbols.doc: Explicit compiler double; never present this record as native validation.

symbols.name: trust_fixture
symbols.doc:
A synthetic installation, its shared toolchain record and the registration request.

The checker identity is the real formal.py, so publication gates recompute a
consistent identity. Each call owns a new directory and record.

symbols.name: trust_environment
symbols.doc:
The instance record and runtime binding that registering this request produces.

Store the record in instance['trust_environments'] and the binding in
runtime['trust_bindings'] under the same ID.

symbols.name: charter_change
symbols.doc: Propose explicit changes to the actual current charter; approval stays public.

symbols.name: charter
symbols.doc: A charter record proposing ``goal``; ``content`` replaces its other content fields. It grants no approval.

symbols.name: charter_record
symbols.doc: Author explicit synthetic charter content; this grants no approval.

symbols.name: approved_governance

contract accepts, built from its actual input: the preparation proposes one

``restore_template`` build: ``count`` ready tasks whose work a real plan selected and queued.

By default: validated active state, a real preparation and sealed contract
approvals, since public activation and contract review have their own tests.
public=True keeps public activation and real reviews for tests whose outcome
depends on that state: check() of synthetic initialization executions
reports an unexamined role input, and activation leaves queue events.

them pending, and the engine would schedule another plan for them. With
count=0 the queue is left as activation left it. Returns the instance ID.
